perspective:
From Ethan Mohamud’s perspective, he has access to:

- He knows his own identity/background: Ethan Mohamud, a plumber, Black, middle-school educated.
- He knows Gary Guo as his long-time close friend from middle school, a doctor, and someone he can support.
- He noticed Gary working excessively long hours at the hospital, often skipping meals and sacrificing sleep.
- He was concerned and invited Gary to a weekend retreat for relaxation and rejuvenation.
- He heard Gary decline at first, saying he had too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, he observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work.
- He suspected there was more behind Gary’s overworking than just professional obligations.
- He confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school, Gary could tell him anything, and he was there to help, not judge.
- He heard Gary say it was complicated and that he did not want to burden Ethan.
- Gary then opened up to him about pressures managing a new department and some personal challenges.
- Ethan felt relief and empathy, and suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities.
- He heard Gary agree and say he could use help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary about his progress and challenges.
- He heard Gary say things were better, that he was less overwhelmed, that he had time for a movie, and that Ethan’s help mattered.
- Ethan felt hopeful and proud, and continued offering support and encouragement.
- After about a year, Ethan saw Gary managing better on his own and decided to step back.
- He told Gary he was always just a call away and knew Gary had things under control.
- He heard Gary thank him, say he could not have done it without Ethan’s support, and that he felt more in control now.

Ethan does not have access to Gary’s unspoken thoughts, private events Ethan did not observe, or narrator-only labels such as Gary’s ISFJ personality type.
